card.title: The stamp that made the sender pay

body.claim: Before the Penny Black, the person receiving a letter in Britain usually paid for it.
body.why: In 1837 British postal rates were high and complicated. It was normal for the recipient to pay on delivery, charged by the sheet and the distance travelled. Sir Rowland Hill proposed an adhesive stamp to show that postage was prepaid. The Penny Black, first issued on 1 May 1840, let a letter of up to half an ounce travel for one penny, whatever the distance.

probes.question: What did the Penny Black change?
options: Only the rich could post letters
The sender prepaid a flat rate, whatever the distance
